RESULTS · PARAGRAPH 2
Knock-in efficiency was stable at 41 ± 3% through passage 16 and collapsed to 4 ± 1% at passage 19 (Figure 2). Viability was unchanged across the series, so the effect is not attributable to cell death. Two reagent lots and a fresh plasmid preparation were tested and neither restored efficiency, which rules out reagent quality as the cause (Rivera, 2026). All gating was performed with gate-and-quantify v1.4.0 following the protocol recorded as MC-0288 v6, unmodified.

DISCUSSION · PARAGRAPH 1
The passage threshold we observe is surprisingly sharpconsistent with a threshold rather than a gradual decline, and it reproduces across two reagent lots. Receptor loss is the most parsimonious explanation, though we did not measure receptor abundance directly in this study. Nucleofection preserves efficiency to at least passage 28T. Okafor, which suggests the limitation is in lipid-mediated uptake specifically.
MLM. LindqvistSUGGESTION18 min ago
Add "in HEK293T" — the Karolinska keratinocyte data does not show this threshold, and a reader will over-generalise.
The practical consequence for laboratories running this protocol is that a low-passage master bank is not an optimisation but a requirement…
